title: Combination of Size-Exclusion Chromatography and Ultracentrifugation for Proteomic Profiling
author: Wei, Zhao, et al.
materials: The principal aim of this study was to improve the proteomic profiling of sEVs from human plasma, under sEVs acquired with higher yield and purity, helping detect and identify novel biomarkers. To compare the isolation efficacy of three methods (UC, SEC, combination of SEC and UC), NTA and MS were employed.

Each protein sample was added 3 μL of 1 μg/μL trypsin and 500 μL of 100 mM TEAB buffer and then digested at 37 °C overnight. Equal volume of 1% formic acid was mixed with digested sample and centrifuged at 12000×g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was slowly loaded to the C18 desalting column, washed with 1 mL of washing solution (0.1% formic acid, 4% acetonitrile) for three times, and then eluted twice by 0.4 mL of elution buffer (0.1% formic acid, 75% acetonitrile). The eluents were combined and lyophilized. The lyophilized protein powder was dissolved in 10 μL 0.1% formic acid in water (solvent A), and then injected into a home-made C18 Nano-Trap column (2 cm × 75 μm, 3 μm). Peptides were separated in a home-made analytical column (15 cm × 150 μm, 1.9 μm) with a mobile phrase of 0.1% formic in 80% acetonitrile (solvent B). Sample elution was performed at a flow rate of 600 nL/min by increasing the solvent B concentration from 6 to 100% over 60 min. The separated peptides were analyzed by Q Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher), with ion source of Nanospray Flex™ (ESI), spray voltage of 2.3 kV.

steps.title: Prepare plasma for UC isolation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge plasma at 3000×g for 15 min, dilute the supernatant 7‑fold with PBS, centrifuge the diluted supernatant at 13 000×g for 30 min, and filter the resulting supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge to pellet sEVs (UC)
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the filtered supernatant using a P50A72–986 rotor (CP100NX; Hitachi) at 150 000×g, 4 °C for 4 h to pellet sEVs.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend UC‑isolated sEVs
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in PBS, ultracentrifuge again at 150 000×g, 4 °C for 2 h, discard the supernatant, and finally resuspend the sEV pellet in 100 μL PBS.

steps.title: Prepare plasma for SEC isolation
steps.instruction: Filter 1 mL fresh plasma through a 0.22 μm filter.

steps.title: Load plasma onto SEC column and elute
steps.instruction: Load the filtered plasma onto a Sepharose‑based CL‑2B column (Echo9103A‑10 ml; ECHO BIOTECH, China) that has been pre‑washed with >20 mL sterile PBS; after the sample has entered the column and no fluid flows from the bottom, elute with PBS, collecting 500 μL fractions.

steps.title: Concentrate SEC fractions and collect sEVs
steps.instruction: Collect fractions 4 through 7 (4 ~ 7 fractions), pool them into a 100 kDa ultrafiltration tube, centrifuge at 4000×g for 15 min, and recover the concentrated sEVs.

steps.title: Combine SEC with UC isolation
steps.instruction: Filter plasma through a 0.22 μm filter, load onto the SEC column as described, collect 2 mL of pooled fractions, then ultracentrifuge at 150 000×g, 4 °C for 4 h; resuspend the pellet in PBS, ultracentrifuge again at 150 000×g, 4 °C for 2 h, discard supernatant and resuspend the final pellet in 100 μL PBS.

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: To each protein sample add 3 μL of 1 μg/μL trypsin and 500 μL of 100 mM TEAB buffer, then incubate at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Acidify, centrifuge and desalt peptides
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 1 % formic acid to the digested sample, centrifuge at 12 000×g for 5 min at room temperature, and load the supernatant onto a C18 desalting column.

substeps.instruction: Wash the column three times with 1 mL washing solution (0.1 % formic acid, 4 % acetonitrile).
Elute twice with 0.4 mL elution buffer (0.1 % formic acid, 75 % acetonitrile).

steps.title: Lyophilize and reconstitute peptides
steps.instruction: Combine the eluates, lyophilize to dryness, then dissolve the lyophilized powder in 10 μL 0.1 % formic acid in water (solvent A).

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS analysis of peptides
steps.instruction: Inject the reconstituted sample onto a home‑made C18 Nano‑Trap column (2 cm × 75 μm, 3 μm) coupled to an analytical column (15 cm × 150 μm, 1.9 μm). Separate peptides using a gradient of solvent B (0.1 % formic acid in 80 % acetonitrile) from 6 % to 100 % over 60 min at a flow rate of 600 nL/min, then analyze on a Q Exactive HF‑X mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher) equipped with a Nanospray Flex™ (ESI) source set to 2.3 kV spray voltage.

steps.title: Search MS data and annotate proteins
steps.instruction: Search raw MS data against the UniProt database, specifying carbamidomethyl as a fixed modification and oxidation of methionine plus N‑terminal acetylation as variable modifications; accept proteins identified with ≥1 unique peptide and a false‑discovery rate ≤0.01, then perform GO, COG and KEGG annotation.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Perform statistical tests in R 3.5.1 (two‑tailed, FDR‑controlled), considering p < 0.05 significant; use the plyr and reshape2 packages for data handling and VennDiagram, pheatmap, and ggplot2 for visualization.
